chunks: And from him, from Abu Ja'far, from his father, and al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the menstruating woman praying over the funeral (body), so he said: 'Yes, and she does not stand with them, and the person in major ritual impurity prays over the funeral (body).'
Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'And the people most entitled to pray over the deceased are those most entitled to his inheritance, until the end of the chapter.'

key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: The person in major ritual impurity
key_terms.وَلَا تَقِفُ مَعَهُمْ: And she does not stand with them (in congregation)

ai.seo_question: Can a menstruating woman pray over a funeral body?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies that menstruating women and those in major ritual impurity (junub) are permitted to perform funeral prayers, though they do not stand in the same row as men, reflecting the distinction between ritual purity and spiritual participation. The concluding remark by Al-Sheikh links the privilege of leading the prayer to inheritance rights, a principle rooted in the Prophet’s tradition that the closest heir leads the funeral rites, emphasizing familial duty over mere ritual cleanliness.
